questions.prompt: From which seat are you making this decision?
questions.why_it_matters: Founders and investors require different prescriptions from the same evidence.
questions.expert_context: I will frame the next action around your actual authority and risk.

questions.prompt: What is the venture's current stage?
questions.why_it_matters: Evidence that is strong at validation may be weak at scaling.
questions.expert_context: The company will be judged against the evidence appropriate to its stage—not a mature-company template.

questions.prompt: Which sector best describes the venture?
questions.why_it_matters: Margins, sales cycles and regulation differ by sector.
questions.expert_context: I will interpret the operating metrics using the right business-model context.

questions.prompt: What is current monthly recurring or repeatable revenue?
questions.why_it_matters: Repeatable revenue is stronger evidence than bookings or isolated pilots.
questions.expert_context: I will treat this as evidence only if its definition is consistent and repeatable.

questions.prompt: What is the recent monthly revenue or active-customer growth rate?
questions.why_it_matters: Growth matters only alongside retention, margin and acquisition quality.
questions.expert_context: I will not reward growth that disappears through churn or uneconomic delivery.

questions.prompt: What percentage of customers or users remain active after the relevant repeat period?
questions.why_it_matters: Retention is evidence that value persists after initial acquisition.
questions.expert_context: This is often more diagnostic than top-line growth because it tests whether the product earns repeated use.

questions.prompt: What is gross margin after direct delivery costs?
questions.why_it_matters: Revenue without viable delivery economics may not create an investable business.
questions.expert_context: I will interpret this relative to sector and stage rather than applying one universal margin target.

questions.prompt: How many months of runway remain at the present burn?
questions.why_it_matters: Runway can override an otherwise attractive score because survival precedes optimisation.
questions.expert_context: If runway is short, the recommendation will prioritise cash preservation and evidence creation.

questions.prompt: How strong is evidence that customers urgently need this?
questions.why_it_matters: Behavioural and paid evidence is stronger than stated enthusiasm.
questions.expert_context: I will distinguish genuine demand evidence from a persuasive founder narrative.

questions.prompt: How complete is the team for the next 18 months?
questions.why_it_matters: Execution risk rises when critical capabilities depend on one person.
questions.expert_context: A team gap may become the next experiment or hiring priority rather than a generic penalty.

questions.prompt: How material is regulatory or compliance uncertainty?
questions.why_it_matters: Unresolved permission or compliance risk can invalidate otherwise good economics.
questions.expert_context: I will treat an unclear regulatory pathway as an evidence gap, not assume it away.
